1 طَفَرَ , (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) aor.
طَفِرَ , (S, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. طُفُورٌ (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and طَفْرٌ, (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) or طَفْرَةٌ, (K,) [but] this has a more particular signification than طَفْرٌ, (Msb,) [being an inf. n. un.,] He leaped: (S:) or he leaped upwards, (Lth, T, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) as when one leaps over a wall to what is behind it. (Lth, T, Mgh, Msb.) One says, طَفَرَ الحَائِطَ, (TA,) or طَفَرَ الحَائِطَ إِلَى مَا وَرَآءَهُ, (A,) He leaped over the wall to what was behind it. (TA.) And طَفَرَ الفَرَسُ النَّهْرَ [The horse leaped over the river, or rivulet]. (A, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
